title: Polynomial representative on the root cube
statement: Let $K$ be a field, let $\omega \in K$, and let $n$ be a natural number. Write $\{1,\omega\}^n$ for the root cube, the set of vectors $x = (x_1,\dots,x_n) \in K^n$ with $x_i \in \{1,\omega\}$ for every $i$. Then for every function $f : \{1,\omega\}^n \to K$ there exists a polynomial $P \in K[X_1,\dots,X_n]$ such that $P(x_1,\dots,x_n) = f(x)$ for all $x$ in the cube.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ a function from the root cube $\{1,\omega\}^n$ to $K$
caveat: The declaration is named "multilinear representative", but the Lean conclusion asserts only the existence of some multivariate polynomial agreeing with $f$ on the cube; it does not require that polynomial to be multilinear, so the prose does not claim multilinearity. The prime $p$ carried in the ambient variables does not appear in the statement and is omitted.
replaced:
Every function $f : \{1,\omega\}^n \to K$ agrees on the cube with the evaluation of some
polynomial $P \in K[X_1,\dots,X_n]$, i.e.\ $P(x) = f(x)$ for all $x$ in the cube.
